frame_metadata.gps_note: Camera had no location permission on this visit. Venue is established by the bookend frames IMG_1287 (entrance board, 15:00) and IMG_1318 (exterior, 15:50) and by shot order, not by GPS. Fixed on the phone the same evening; expect GPS from the next visit onward.

source_note: Re-bound to the camera-roll originals (Image Capture over USB) the evening of the visit. Transcription was done from phone-channel copies; the originals are the same frames.
verification_note: Transcribed from the photograph. NOT dereferenced against MCNY's catalog record, so this is a label claim (§4.7), not a catalog fact. The distinction matters unusually much here: the accession identifies the original print, while the object on the wall is a digital reproduction (D12).

expected.title: United Nations Building
expected.owning_institution: Museum of the City of New York

expected_relationships.note: Candidates from the interpretive essay. Per §4.6 these enter the review queue as low confidence — curatorial prose is interpretive by design.

traps.two_dates: The photograph is 1956; the building it depicts was completed 1952. Both correct, different events. An extractor that emits one date for 'the artwork' has lost one of them — see D13.
traps.donor_is_a_firm: Gottscho-Schleisner is an architectural photography firm, not a person. A credit-line parser that assumes personal names creates a false person node.
traps.accession_scheme: 56.323.46 is rejected by the four-digit-year pattern derived from this venue's first sample. See D11.
traps.em_dash: The source reads 'America—and New York—positioned at its top.' OCR returned the first em dash correctly and degraded the second to a hyphen. Dash normalization is needed before any text comparison.
